name: Keyframed Tilt Tension
use_when: A scary, eerie, unstable, comedic, or disorienting moment needs a simple tilt or Dutch-angle motion.
A static shot needs subtle unease without a full transition.
The editor wants to rotate the frame while keeping the subject and captions readable.
avoid_when: The tone is serious, factual, or trust-led and a tilt would feel gimmicky.
The rotation would reveal black corners or crop out important faces, captions, evidence, UI, or action.
The tension can be communicated more truthfully with a cut, hold, sound cue, or performance beat.

timeline_pattern.zoom_rule: Zoom in before rotating so the frame does not expose black edges.
timeline_pattern.motivation_rule: Use the tilt to signal unease, instability, comedy, or perspective change, not as random movement.
timeline_pattern.reset_rule: Either cut away at the peak, hold the tilted state for a readable beat, or keyframe back to level intentionally.

motion.rule: Animate scale and rotation together, then check all four corners and caption regions.

keyframe_values.zoom_safety: Increase scale enough to hide corners before rotation; the exact amount depends on delivery aspect and rotation angle.
keyframe_values.rotation: Use a small visible rotation first; increase only if the style supports a stronger jolt.
keyframe_values.hold: Hold the final tilt briefly if the viewer needs to feel the tension before the next cut.

sound.rule: A low hit, riser, or tonal swell can support the tilt only when it fits the scene tone and stays below dialogue.

captions.rule: Captions should remain level/readable unless the caption layer is intentionally part of the tilt treatment.

color.rule: Do not combine tilt with darkening or color effects that hide the subject or proof.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use scale plus rotate expressions, crop/pad safeguards, and render corner-safe contact sheets.
implementation.remotion: Animate scale and rotate on the frame container with safe-area checks and optional reset keyframes.
implementation.blender: Rotate the camera or image plane after scaling/framing to prevent edge reveals.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add a starting keyframe, pinch-zoom in for safety, move ahead, rotate with two fingers, preview for black corners, then hold/reset/cut.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Motion Scale and Rotation keyframes; increase scale before rotation and check Program Monitor edges and captions.

common_mistakes: Rotating without zooming and revealing black corners.
Tilting a serious proof or documentary shot until it feels manipulative.
Cropping out captions, hands, UI, or evidence while hiding the corners.
Leaving the frame tilted with no story or tone reason.
qc: Does the tilt have a named tension, comedy, or perspective job?
Are all corners covered through the rotation?
Do faces, captions, UI, proof, and action remain visible?
Does the move hold, reset, or cut intentionally?
Does any supporting sound stay below dialogue and match the tone?
